sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles a short stretch of the southern Apennines in the Irpinia area, just north of the high Sele R. valley. This source is a high-angle, SW-dipping, normal fault system just east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable destructive seismicity within the area. These earthquakes are the 8 September 1694 (Mw 6.9, Irpinia-Basilicata) and the well known multiple earthquake of 23 November 1980 (Mw 6.9, Irpinia-Basilicata).
This source lies within the whole NW-SE striking extensional axis of the southern Apennines. It is primarily formed by the SW-dipping fault that caused the third event of the well studied 1980 multiple earthquake, a seismic sequence that has shown a mechanism of normal fault interaction in this region. On its northeastern border, this source gives way to the crustal volume including the causative fault (to date unknown and puzzling) of the 1694 earthquake. On its southwestern border, this source interacts with the much larger antithetic, SW-dipping normal fault system that includes the sources of the first and second sub-events of the 1980 earthquake.
The main segment of this Source has been associated with the third sub-event of the 1980 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents pure extension, based on geological and seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. The slip rate was based on paleoseismological data.

evidence: Inferred from depth of major earthquakes of the region.
Based on seismological and macroseismic data.
